title: Friday Night Behind the Bar
briefing: The bar is filling up. Chill a glass, pour the cocktail and get it to the guest at the service counter.

lines.intro: Ice the glass, pour the gin, and send it to the service counter.
lines.done: Clean pour. The guests are happy.

lines.intro: A gin cocktail when you get a second, please!

objectives.label: Grab a cocktail glass
objectives.tip: Hold glasses by the stem or base, never by the rim.

objectives.label: Set the glass in the ice well
objectives.tip: A chilled glass keeps a stirred drink cold and crisp for longer.

objectives.label: Chill the glass with ice
objectives.tip: Fill the glass right to the top with ice. More ice melts slower.

objectives.label: Take the chilled glass
objectives.tip: Tip out the ice and meltwater before you pour.

objectives.label: Put the glass on the cocktail station
objectives.tip: Build drinks on the bar mat so spills stay off the bar top.

objectives.label: Grab the gin
objectives.tip: Read the label every time. The wrong spirit means a remake.

objectives.label: Set the bottle at the pour spot
objectives.tip: Keep bottles label out so you and the guest can both see them.

objectives.label: Pour a measured shot
objectives.tip: Use a jigger for every pour. Even measures keep drinks and costs right.

objectives.label: Pick up the cocktail
objectives.tip: Hold it low on the stem so your hand does not warm the drink.

objectives.label: Serve it at the service counter
objectives.tip: Set it on a napkin in front of the guest, facing them.

announce.text: Dev moved down the bar. Serve it at the far end of the counter instead, then let him know.

replaceRemaining.label: Pick up the cocktail
replaceRemaining.tip: Hold it low on the stem so your hand does not warm the drink.

replaceRemaining.label: Serve it at the far end of the counter
replaceRemaining.tip: Keep track of where every guest sits. Guests move all night.

replaceRemaining.label: Let Dev know his drink is ready
replaceRemaining.tip: Make eye contact and name the drink as you hand it over.

facts: A standard shot is measured with a jigger, usually 1.5 ounces in North America.
Chilling the glass keeps a cocktail cold without extra dilution.
Bartenders often need a responsible-serving certification to pour alcohol.

order.text: A gin cocktail in a chilled glass
order.waiting: Any chance that gin is coming soon?

career.dayInLife: Set up before doors open: cut garnishes, stock ice and bottles, check the kegs. Then serve a busy room for hours while checking IDs and watching how much guests drink. After close, clean, count the till and restock.
career.schedule: Evenings, late nights and weekends, often finishing after midnight.

physical.note: Standing for hours and lifting ice, kegs and cases.

people.note: Talking with guests all night, reading moods, refusing service.

pressure.note: Rushes stack orders, and you must stay accurate and calm.

hard: Late nights that throw off your sleep
Handling guests who have had too much
career.start: You must be of legal serving age. Many start as barbacks. A responsible alcohol service certificate is often required.
